# Lab 18.1: IAM for BigQuery

## What We Are Going to Do
Grant BigQuery roles at project, dataset and table level to a test service account, and test what it can and cannot do.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a dataset, two tables and a test identity.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab18
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'CREATE TABLE lab18.sales AS SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` LIMIT 1000'
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'CREATE TABLE lab18.salaries AS SELECT "Asha" AS name, 90000 AS salary'
gcloud iam service-accounts create bq-analyst --display-name="BQ test analyst"
export ANALYST=bq-analyst@$PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding $ANALYST \
  --member="user:$(gcloud config get-value account)" --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Let the analyst run jobs (project level).**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$ANALYST --role=roles/bigquery.jobUser --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   `jobUser` lets you run queries but gives no access to any data.

3. **[SQL] Grant read access to one table only.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">GRANT `roles/bigquery.dataViewer`
ON TABLE lab18.sales
TO "serviceAccount:bq-analyst@YOUR_PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com";</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[CLI] Test as the analyst.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account $ANALYST
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab18.sales'      # works
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT * FROM lab18.salaries'          # Access Denied
gcloud config unset auth/impersonate_service_account</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Grant at dataset level.** Open `lab18 → Sharing → Permissions → Add principal`. Give the analyst **BigQuery Data Viewer** on the whole dataset. Repeat step 4: now both tables work.

6. **[Console] Remove the dataset grant** to go back to table-level access only.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `jobUser` | Run queries, no data access |
| `dataViewer` on a table | Read that table only |
| Dataset grant | Read every table in the dataset |
| Principle | Least privilege |
